# Citation, Edition, and License {.unnumbered}

This page identifies the publication status, preferred citation, versioning conventions, repository record, and licensing information for *Machine Learning Using Python*.

## Publication Identity

**Title:** *Machine Learning Using Python*  
**Subtitle:** *Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research*  
**Author:** Itauma Itauma  
**ORCID:** [0009-0000-8835-5292](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-8835-5292)  
**Edition:** Second Edition  
**Version:** 2.0.0  
**Publication date:** August 28, 2026  
**Publication format:** Quarto book and reproducible computational repository  
**Canonical DOI:** [10.5281/zenodo.22136083](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22136083)

The Second Edition contains **18 chapters organized into six parts**, together with front matter, teaching resources, author information, references, and publication metadata.

## Preferred Citation

Please cite the archived Second Edition as:

> Itauma, I. (2026). *Machine Learning Using Python: Foundations, Algorithms, Applications, and Reproducible Research* (2nd ed., Version 2.0.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22136083

The DOI identifies the preserved Second Edition release and should be preferred when citing the book as a scholarly object.

## Versioning

The book uses versioned releases so that readers can distinguish the evolving repository from a fixed scholarly release.

The publication record distinguishes among:

- the **edition** of the book;
- the **version** of a specific release;
- the **Git tag** associated with that release;
- the **archival DOI** assigned to the preserved release.

These identifiers serve different purposes.

The **Second Edition** identifies the intellectual edition of the book. Version **2.0.0** identifies this release. The Git tag **v2.0.0** identifies the corresponding repository snapshot. The DOI identifies the archived scholarly object.

The release relationship is:

$$
\text{Second Edition}
\rightarrow
\text{Version 2.0.0}
\rightarrow
\text{Git tag v2.0.0}
\rightarrow
\text{Archived Release}
\rightarrow
\text{DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22136083}.
$$

## Repository and Reproducibility

The source files, executable examples, environment information, and reproducibility infrastructure for the Second Edition are maintained with the book repository:

<https://github.com/amightyo/machine-learning-using-python-2e>

The browsable HTML edition is available at:

<https://amightyo.github.io/machine-learning-using-python-2e/>

The repository is intended to support:

- transparent inspection of the source;
- reproducible execution of examples;
- version history;
- issue tracking and corrections;
- preservation of release-specific materials.

Readers reproducing computational results should consult the environment and reproducibility documentation associated with the release they are using.

## Archival DOI

The canonical DOI for the Second Edition, Version 2.0.0, is:

**DOI:** [10.5281/zenodo.22136083](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22136083)

This DOI is the preferred persistent identifier for the archived Second Edition.

## License

The book separates the licensing of original educational content from any third-party materials that may appear through citation, quotation, datasets, software packages, documentation, or other attributed resources.

Book prose, original figures, exercises, and other non-code educational content are licensed under the **Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)** license. Original executable source code is licensed under the **MIT License**, as documented in the repository license file.

Third-party materials remain subject to their respective licenses, terms, and attribution requirements.

## How to Cite Code or a Specific Release

When reproducibility requires identifying the exact computational state used for an analysis, cite the archived release or version corresponding to that state rather than citing only the continuously updated repository.

A reproducible citation record should make it possible to identify:

1. the book edition;
2. the release version;
3. the repository snapshot or Git tag;
4. the archival DOI.

This distinction matters because computational dependencies, examples, corrections, and supporting materials can evolve after publication.

## Corrections and Updates

Corrections made after this archival release should be documented through subsequent repository history and, when appropriate, a new versioned release.

A corrected release should preserve the scholarly record rather than silently replacing the state associated with an earlier archived version.

## Citation Principle

The purpose of citation metadata is not merely formatting.

It is provenance.

$$
\boxed{\text{A Scholarly Artifact Should Be Identifiable, Recoverable, and Verifiable}}
$$

The publication record for the Second Edition connects the rendered book, source repository, versioned release, and archival DOI.
